cleanIntro: The Model 24 is Savage's combination gun: a rifle barrel over a shotgun barrel on one break-open frame, fired by a single exposed hammer whose built-in selector picks the barrel, with a crossbolt hammer block through the frame as the safety. The teardown is short — forend screw out, forend off, top lever over, barrel down and out of the frame. Savage's book for this gun covers serial numbers E963107 and above; check yours before you rely on it.

steps.title: Check the serial — this book is for E963107 and above
steps.action: Look at the serial number on your frame before you take anything apart. Savage's Model 24 book prints its own coverage line: serial E963107 and above. The Model 24 was built for decades in many versions, and an older gun is not covered by this procedure just because the name on the barrel matches. If your serial is below that number, stop here and find the book for your gun.
steps.prose: The parts list in the same book also names the Model 24F, which shares this takedown.
steps.cite: Savage Arms — Instruction Manual — MODEL 24 Combination Rifle/Shotgun — UNKNOWN — no part number, revision code or date code is printed anywhere in this document — To Assemble Gun, PDF p.2 (no folio printed)

steps.title: Hammer down, in the safe position
steps.action: Check the hammer before anything else. On this gun the hammer's safe position is fully forward, with a visible gap between the selector in the hammer and the firing pins — resting there, the firing pin does not touch a primer. A cocked hammer is the one state in which this gun is ready to fire, so if the hammer is back, do not open the action until it has been brought safely down as Savage's unload procedure describes.
steps.prose: Savage wants the gun carried this way at all times until you are ready to shoot.
steps.quote: The hammer on this rifle/shotgun is in the SAFE POSITION when it is in the forward position with a space between the selector and the firing pins
steps.cite: Savage Arms — Instruction Manual — MODEL 24 Combination Rifle/Shotgun — UNKNOWN — no part number, revision code or date code is printed anywhere in this document — Operating Instructions, PDF p.2 (no folio printed)

steps.title: Crossbolt to the right — red band hidden
steps.action: Find the crossbolt hammer block through the frame. Pushed to the left it exposes a red band, and that red band means the gun is set to fire. For cleaning it stays pushed to the right, sticking out of the right side of the frame with no red showing. If you see red, push it back to the right before you go further.
steps.prose: The crossbolt blocks the hammer; it is a supplement to keeping the hammer down, not a substitute.
steps.quote: move crossbolt to the left exposing the red band which indicates the firing position.
steps.cite: Savage Arms — Instruction Manual — MODEL 24 Combination Rifle/Shotgun — UNKNOWN — no part number, revision code or date code is printed anywhere in this document — Safety Instructions, Crossbolt Hammer Block, PDF p.2 (no folio printed)

steps.title: Open the action and take both shells out
steps.action: Muzzle in a safe direction, open the action with the top lever and lift out whatever is in either chamber — the rifle barrel on top and the shotgun barrel below are separate chambers and each must be checked. Then look through both barrels from the breech end. Do not close the action again with a shell in it; from here on the gun should be empty and open.
steps.prose: A combination gun loaded in one barrel only is the easy one to miss.
steps.quote: Open the action and remove shells.
steps.cite: Savage Arms — Instruction Manual — MODEL 24 Combination Rifle/Shotgun — UNKNOWN — no part number, revision code or date code is printed anywhere in this document — To Uncock or Unload, PDF p.3 (no folio printed)

steps.title: Forend screw out, forend off
steps.action: With the gun confirmed empty and the hammer down, remove the forend screw. Grasp the front of the forend and pull it away from the barrel. Keep the screw with the forend so it cannot roll off the bench — it is the only thing that holds the forend on.
steps.prose: The forend is what keeps the barrel on the frame once the action opens.
steps.caution: MAKE SURE THE GUN IS UNLOADED
steps.quote: pull the forend away from the barrel.
steps.cite: Savage Arms — Instruction Manual — MODEL 24 Combination Rifle/Shotgun — UNKNOWN — no part number, revision code or date code is printed anywhere in this document — To Disassemble Gun, PDF p.2 (no folio printed)

steps.title: Top lever over, barrel down and out of the frame
steps.action: Hold the barrel and the action firmly, one in each hand. Press the top lever to the right or left to open the action, and keep rotating the barrel downward until its lug comes out of the front of the frame. With the forend off nothing else holds it, so keep your grip on the barrel the whole way.
steps.prose: Two pieces now: the barrel assembly and the stock-and-frame.
steps.quote: rotating the barrel down and out of the frame.
steps.cite: Savage Arms — Instruction Manual — MODEL 24 Combination Rifle/Shotgun — UNKNOWN — no part number, revision code or date code is printed anywhere in this document — To Disassemble Gun, PDF p.2 (no folio printed)

steps.title: Keep this barrel with this frame
steps.action: Savage fits the barrel and frame to each other at the factory. If more than one Model 24 lives in your house, keep each barrel with its own frame and never swap them, even if they seem to go together. A barrel on the wrong frame can lock up badly enough to be dangerous.
steps.prose: Savage warns that switching barrels or frames can cause serious damage or injury.
steps.quote: The barrel and frame are a matched set from the factory.
steps.cite: Savage Arms — Instruction Manual — MODEL 24 Combination Rifle/Shotgun — UNKNOWN — no part number, revision code or date code is printed anywhere in this document — To Assemble Gun, PDF p.2 (no folio printed)

steps.title: Both bores, until the patch comes out clean
steps.action: With the barrel off, run a patch wet with solvent through each bore, then a brass brush soaked in solvent through the full length several times with long, even strokes. Follow with clean patches until the last one comes out unsoiled, then one lightly oiled patch through the whole bore. Do the rifle barrel and the shotgun barrel each in turn — they take different brushes and patches.
steps.prose: Check both bores for a stuck patch before anything goes back together.
steps.caution: A barrel does not have to be completely blocked to cause a barrel rupture.
steps.quote: Push clean patches through the bore in the same manner until the last patch comes out unsoiled.
steps.cite: Savage Arms — Instruction Manual — MODEL 24 Combination Rifle/Shotgun — UNKNOWN — no part number, revision code or date code is printed anywhere in this document — How To Care For Your Firearm, PDF p.5 (no folio printed)

steps.title: Breech face and extractors, brush and solvent
steps.action: Brush or blow loose residue out of the action area. Then, with a brush and solvent, clean the breech face on the frame and the extractors on the barrel. Wipe them dry afterwards and leave only a light film of oil.
steps.prose: This is where fouling from both barrels collects.
steps.quote: Also with a brush and solvent clean the breech face and extractors.
steps.cite: Savage Arms — Instruction Manual — MODEL 24 Combination Rifle/Shotgun — UNKNOWN — no part number, revision code or date code is printed anywhere in this document — How To Care For Your Firearm, PDF p.5 (no folio printed)

steps.title: Choke tube — gun open and empty, clean seat, snug
steps.action: If your shotgun barrel takes choke tubes, check that the gun is unloaded and leave it open while you change one. Make sure the threads and the seat for the tube are clean, free of debris and not damaged. Fit the tube with the supplied wrench and tighten it snugly against the seat once it touches. A tube that is not seated can let gas and shot get between the tube and the barrel and ruin both.
steps.prose: Savage marks its tubes with notches on the outer edge so you can read the choke without taking it out.
steps.quote: Open the gun and check to see that it is not loaded and leave open while changing choke tubes.
steps.cite: Savage Arms — Instruction Manual — MODEL 24 Combination Rifle/Shotgun — UNKNOWN — no part number, revision code or date code is printed anywhere in this document — Choke Tube Installation, PDF p.4 (no folio printed)

steps.title: Oil the metal lightly — but never the locking bolt
steps.action: Wipe all metal parts dry and oil them lightly. Leave the locking bolt dry: Savage warns that oil on it can let the action partly open. Between seasons, put a coat of oil in the bore and on the metal parts and store the gun somewhere dry, never with the barrel plugged and never in a fabric case that soaks the oil off the metal.
steps.prose: The locking bolt is the part that holds the barrel closed against the frame.
steps.quote: NOTE: DO NOT OIL LOCKING BOLT AS THIS MAY CAUSE ACTION TO PARTIALLY OPEN.
steps.cite: Savage Arms — Instruction Manual — MODEL 24 Combination Rifle/Shotgun — UNKNOWN — no part number, revision code or date code is printed anywhere in this document — How To Care For Your Firearm, PDF p.5 (no folio printed)

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Barrel assembly, forend with its screw, and the stock-and-frame: that is the whole Model 24 teardown Savage publishes. The hammer, selector, crossbolt, locking bolt, extractors and trigger stay where they are. Savage puts any trigger adjustment in the hands of an authorized gunsmith and asks for the gun to be checked periodically by a competent gunsmith, so there is no deeper branch to walk here.
steps.prose: With the forend off, look over the barrel's underside and the forend for cracks or wear.
steps.quote: This firearm should be checked periodically by a competent gunsmith to insure proper operation
steps.cite: Savage Arms — Instruction Manual — MODEL 24 Combination Rifle/Shotgun — UNKNOWN — no part number, revision code or date code is printed anywhere in this document — Further Care, PDF p.5 (no folio printed)

deepAbsentReason: Savage's Model 24 book ends at the takedown: forend screw out, forend off, and the barrel rotated down and out of the frame (To Disassemble Gun, PDF p.2; the book prints no page numbers). It prints no hammer, selector, locking bolt, extractor or trigger teardown. It reserves trigger work to a gunsmith — "NOTE: ADJUSTMENTS MADE TO THE TRIGGER ASSEMBLY MUST BE PERFORMED BY AN AUTHORIZED GUNSMITH" (PDF p.4) — and sends periodic checks and the replacement of worn parts to a competent gunsmith (Further Care, PDF p.5). The parts list on PDF p.7 is for ordering parts, not a procedure.

cleaning.name: BORES — RIFLE AND SHOTGUN BARRELS
tasks: Action open, barrel off the frame
Patch wet with solvent through each bore
Brass brush soaked in solvent, full length, several long even strokes
Clean patches until the last one comes out unsoiled
One lightly oiled patch through the whole bore
Do the rifle barrel and the shotgun barrel each in turn
Check both bores for obstructions before reassembly

cleaning.name: BREECH FACE & EXTRACTORS
tasks: Brush or blow residue out of the action area
Brush and solvent on the breech face
Brush and solvent on the extractors
Wipe dry and oil lightly

cleaning.name: CHOKE TUBE
tasks: Gun unloaded and left open while changing a choke tube
Threads and seat clean, free of debris and not damaged
Fit with the supplied wrench; tighten snugly once it contacts the seat
⚠ A tube that is not seated can ruin the tube and the barrel

cleaning.name: METAL & STORAGE
tasks: Wipe all metal parts dry and oil lightly
⛔ Do not oil the locking bolt — it can let the action partly open
Between seasons: coat of oil in the bore and on metal parts, store dry
Do not plug the barrel
Do not store in a fabric case that soaks up the oil

reassembly: Make sure the hammer is in the safe position.
Holding the rear of the gun in one hand and the barrel in the other, link the barrel lug into the front of the frame.
Pivot the barrel upward until it locks with the frame.
Hold the rear of the forend against the frame, insert the forend screw and tighten it.
fncheck: With both chambers confirmed empty, open and close the action and check that the barrel locks up firmly to the frame and the top lever returns to its place. Push the crossbolt hammer block to the left and confirm the red band shows, then back to the right and confirm it is hidden — leave it on the right. With the hammer down, move the selector in the hammer up and down and confirm it moves to each position. Look through both bores from the breech end once more for a patch left behind. If the action does not lock up fully, or anything feels different from usual, the gun goes to a gunsmith before it is fired.
